Reverse charged

Reverse-charged tax codes are used when the recipient of goods or services is responsible for paying the tax instead of the supplier. This commonly occurs in cross-border transactions and certain domestic business-to-business supplies.

Configure reporting categories to ensure reverse-charged tax amounts appear correctly on your tax returns. These categories help organize transactions where you act as both the supplier and the tax collector.

When you purchase goods or services subject to reverse charge, the system will calculate the tax you owe while simultaneously allowing you to claim it back as input tax, resulting in a net zero effect for VAT-registered businesses.

Proper categorization is essential for accurate VAT and GST reporting, as reverse-charged amounts must be reported in specific sections of your tax return to comply with tax authority requirements.
